subject: Post-call: token runway & batching tradeoffs — next steps
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia@finrise.co>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finrise.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: token runway & batching tradeoffs — next steps

Hi Lydia / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a proposed path forward so your finance/CFO can react quickly.

What we heard
- Primary pain: token spend volatility during month-end reconciliation flows (large batch requests) and occasional latency spikes that impact UX.
- Goal: prove production-quality inference for the reconciliation use case with clear unit economics (pilot should demonstrate < $12K/month run rate at target throughput).
- Constraints: CFO wants a hard budget guardrail; security/compliance review (SOC2 docs) is required before production.

High-level recommended pilot (we discussed):
- Scope: Redwood-hosted pilot, 6-week window, 1 model endpoint, 2 routes (inference for short summaries + detailed reconciliation).
- SLOs: target 250ms P95 for short summaries; allow higher latency for detailed runs.
- Levers to hit budget: batching (dynamic 25-75ms threshold), prefix/KV caching for repeated invoice prompts (we saw ~65% reuse on similar workloads), and a quantized model variant for the detail route.

Ballpark economics (very approximate — will refine with logs):
- Ballpark token run: 10–12M tokens/month for pilot at current volume assumptions.
- With batching + cache we estimate ~45% token-cost reduction vs naive per-request serving; expected host costs ~ $9–11K/month.

Attachments: redwood_pilot_pricing_v2.pdf (pricing + two pilot sizing scenarios).

Next steps / asks
1) Can you confirm the CFO budget guardrail (is $12K/month acceptable as a pilot ceiling?)
2) Can you share a small sample of end-of-month traffic (anonymized request/response sizes) — helps us tighten estimate.
3) Would next Tuesday (11/11) at 10am PT work for a short SOW + ops playbook review?

If that’s all good I’ll loop in Diego (SE) and Marissa (pricing) to firm up a tight pilot configuration and a one-page SOW your finance team can sign.

Thanks —
Michael Grant
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
michael@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks Michael — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The CFO is firm about a pilot ceiling — $12k/month max. We could stretch for a clear business case but need prior sign-off before any overage.
- For volume: we expect ~100k inference requests/month during pilot but with big variance (end-of-month windows bump by ~3x for ~48 hours).
- Latency: 250ms P95 for the short summary route is a hard requirement for product. Longer detail route can be slower.

I’ll work on a small anonymized sample of the heavy window logs — should have that by Friday. Also please send your SOC2 docs link so our security team can start the review in parallel.

Tuesday 11/11 10am PT works for a call to review SOW.

Marissa / Diego — forwarding the FinRise recap and their constraints. Key asks: they have a hard pilot ceiling of $12K/month and require 250ms P95 on the short route. They can provide a traffic sample by Friday.

My suggested pilot config to hit their guardrail (initial pass):
- Mode: Redwood-hosted dedicated endpoint with autoscale cap (to contain run-rate).
- Batching: target 25ms dynamic allow-window, max accumulation 50ms for short-route; larger window for the detail route.
- Caching: aggressive prefix KV caching for invoice templates (~65% reuse assumed).
- Model: short-route -> optimized small open model quantized (faster and cheaper); detailed -> 7B quantized variant.
- Ops: 6-week pilot, 2-week canary with throttles and budget alerting; hard budget cap configured to stop autoscaling beyond $12K/month.

Ballpark cost with these levers (back-of-envelope): $9.5K/month. If traffic variance is higher, we may need to tighten batching/quantization further or propose a staged commit from FinRise.

Marissa — can you confirm pricing/discounting to fit $12K guardrail and draft a minimal SOW? Diego — can you validate the latency feasibility for the short route under the suggested batching/caching assumptions (250ms P95) and note any risks/mitigations?

Forwarded message follows below.

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2025 09:05:00 -0700

Thanks — quick technical readout:

- 250ms P95 for short summaries is feasible with the proposed setup assuming: batch accumulation target <= 30ms, prefix cache hit rate >= 60%, and the short-route uses the quantized 3–4B optimized variant.
- Risk windows: the 48-hour end-of-month spike could push queueing; we should plan a temporary request shed strategy (route-based rate limiting + a smaller fallback model) and a hard autoscale budget cap to prevent runaway spend.
- Ops checklist: I attached pilot_ops_checklist.md — includes throttles, budget alert thresholds, and rollback playbook.

I’ll run a quick internal perf sim when they send the sample logs and report back — expect results within 48 hours of receiving samples.
